data.title: Compatibility and deprecation policy
body: # Compatibility and deprecation policy
What kadence promises about the data it leaves in your repository, and how it
changes without breaking that. Written 2026-10-01 for gate G3 (DOC-32): the
category's users leave tools whose upgrades lose their data, so this is the
promise 1.0 is made of.
## What the contract is
- **The event format** — every `FlowEvent`: its fields and its `type`s.
- **The `.kadence/` layout** — one event per file under `.kadence/events/`,
archives, `README.md`; `state.json` is a cache and not part of it (I6).
- **The `--json` contract** — `schema: "kadence/v1"`, the fields
`kadence schema --json` lists, error codes, exit codes.
## Inside `kadence/v1`: additive only
- Event types, event fields, commands, flags, JSON fields and error codes may
be **added**. Nothing is renamed or removed.
- An older kadence that meets an event type it does not know **skips it and
counts it** (`unknownTypes`) rather than failing; the state degrades to what
it knew, never to something wrong.
- A changed **default** (what a command does without a flag) is allowed, and
is announced under "⚠️ Upgrading" in the CHANGELOG with the flag that gives
the old behaviour (0.7.0 and 0.8.0 did this).
## Old journals keep reading the same
- A journal written by **any released version** folds, with every later
version, into what that version itself reported. `test/compatibility.test.ts`
holds this on real journals from every minor version since 0.1, made by
`scripts/make-fixtures.mjs` with the published packages.
- **Every release adds its own fixture**: after publishing, run
`node scripts/make-fixtures.mjs <version>` and commit the result.
## Migration is new events, never rewriting
The journal is append-only (DEC-44): no command edits or deletes an event, and
no upgrade rewrites one. When the meaning of the data has to change, the new
meaning arrives as new events that later code folds; the old events stay
readable for as long as the repository exists.
## Deprecation
- A command, flag or JSON field marked deprecated keeps working for **at least
two minor releases and at least 90 days**, whichever is longer.
- It is announced in three places: the CHANGELOG under "Deprecated", its
`--help`, and a warning on stderr when used — never on stdout, which is JSON
only under `--json`.
- `kadence schema --json` will mark it with a `deprecated` field — added, additively, with the first deprecation; none has happened yet.
## Breaking changes
- **Before 1.0:** a 0.x release may break the contract only with a "⚠️"
section in the CHANGELOG that says what changed and how to get the old
behaviour. None has needed to break the event format so far.
- **From 1.0:** only in a new major version, with a new schema name
(`kadence/v2`), and with both readable through a stated transition.
